text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed ~30% token/sec drop on canary after the 11:00 deploy. Queue depth jumped and CTB drain times are way higher.
mina: ugh, saw alerts. Is this across all models or specific to long-seq traffic?
alex: Mostly long-seq (2k+), but small-batch latency also increased a bit. KV hitrate looks normal-ish but avg batch size dropped.
jon: I grabbed a perf trace from canary. Top of stack is heavy memcpy on kernel selection path. Flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/fg/2460032 — big spike in kernel->memcpy when CTB coalesces.
sam: Any recent kernel-selection or quantization policy PRs?
mina: PR #1328 from earlier today changed the kernel fallback ordering for q8_hybrid -> q8_fast for certain seqlen heuristics. That touched selection heuristics in scheduler.
perf-ci-bot: perf-run/job/ctb-throughput/2460032 completed — regression detected: tokens/sec baseline 18.4k -> canary 12.9k (-29.9%). CI artifacts: https://ci.redwood/artifacts/2460032
jon: I ran `git bisect` locally across the last 10 merges, narrowed to merge c7a9f3d (merge PR #1328). Reproduces on dev rig with synthetic 2k sequences.
mina: OK thx. Can we reproduce with kvcache disabled to isolate?
alex: Disabled KV: token/sec drop still present but reduced to -15%. So KV interaction amplifies it but not sole cause.
sam: So two factors: kernel-selection change increases memcopy overhead, and CTB batching pattern now creates more small batches (lost coalescing) leading to lower average batch size.
jon: Profiling call stacks: shows increased time in `choose_kernel()` and `memcopy_dispatch()` when `seqlen_threshold` condition hits. Patch in #1328 flips the threshold check order.
mina: I pushed a quick diagnostic build that logs kernel choices and batch sizes. Logs show lots of q8_fast chosen for 2k sequences where previously we used q8_hybrid. q8_fast ends up doing an extra memcpy path on this hardware.
infra-bot: Canary metrics: 12:10 -> queueing latency p95 jumped from 36ms -> 102ms, inflight batch size p50 dropped 1.8 -> 1.1.
alex: We should probably hold rollout. Any easy rollback?
sam: Reverting the selection change is a small PR (Revert PR #1328). I can open it now.
mina: Before reverting, could we try a kernel-hint override at routing level to force q8_hybrid for long-seq canary instances? Might be faster than full revert.
jon: Tried override on one canary node: tokens/sec returned to 18.0k, queueing p95 back to ~40ms. So override fixes it.
perf-ci-bot: perf-run/job/ctb-throughput/2460033 (with kernel-hint override) — tokens/sec 18.1k (pass).
mina: Good repro + quick mitigation. Sam, open revert but we'll hold until revert lands. Apply kernel-hint override to all canaries to stop user impact.
sam: Revert PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/rt-infer/pull/1335 (revert of #1328). I'll also push the kernel-hint rollout config change to canary groups.
alex: Can someone add a regression test in CI that exercises CTB coalescing for long sequences and asserts no memcopy surge?
jon: On it — adding a micro-benchmark that runs 1k 2k-seq requests in CTB mode and compares per-token memcpy bytes. Will run in perf gate.
mina: After override applied, metrics look stable. We'll keep canary paused and wait for revert CI to pass.
perf-ci-bot: CI pipeline for revert PR #1335 started: build/bench/2460040.
sam: If revert CI passes, we will roll through staged canary -> prod after monitoring window. If revert fails, we'll rollback/rollback-rollback: :grimacing:
alex: Thanks everyone. Good catch. Please paste short postmortem once root-cause confirmed (kernel selection ordering + CTB heuristics interaction causing memcopy path and batch undercoalescing).
mina: Will write a quick incident note and link perf traces + bisect.
jon: Flames + profiles uploaded: https://perf.redwood/uploads/2460032-profiles.tar.gz
alex: Closing loop — revert merged and rolled to canary at 15:40. Current tokens/sec back to baseline ~18.3k. Will keep monitoring for 2h. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Alert cleared at 15:55. Canary queueing p95 stabilized at 38ms.
sam: Follow-up tasks: (1) add perf gate micro-bench (jon), (2) add automated CTB kernel-hint smoke (mina), (3) add regression detection in nightly perf for memcopy bytes (alex).
mina: Adding tasks to sprint board.
jon: I'll include a short doc on why q8_hybrid avoided memcpy on this hw (few lines + assembly note).
alex: Great, thanks team.
